Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 738 PM EDT Wed Oct 14 2026

- Temperatures closer to normal and drier today, followed by
  additional rainfall late Thursday afternoon into early Friday
  morning.

- A strong cold front delivers gusty winds and much chillier
  conditions Friday, with a few showers in spots.

- Turing drier through the weekend with slightly warmer readings by
  Sunday.

&&

.AVIATION...

High pressure will slide across Lake Superior overnight, reaching 
eastern Ontario Thursday morning. This leads to veering low level 
winds, which redirects low level moisture back into SE Michigan to 
maintain a mix of low VFR and MVFR conditions through the TAF 
period. Low pressure organizes over the Plains Thursday morning and 
then lifts northeast into the Great Lakes region by Thursday night. 
Increasing southeast flow emerges ahead of the low with potential 
for shower development as the elevated warm front lifts in. There is 
a low chance for an elevated thunderstorm to develop as lapse rates 
approach 6.0 C/km above the inversion, although too low of 
confidence to include in the TAF at this time. Ceilings then lower 
into Thursday night. 

D21/DTW Convection...No thunderstorms before 22Z Thursday, low 
chance after 22z. 

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Medium for ceilings at or below 5000 feet this evening. High late
  tonight and Thursday. 

* Low for thunder after 22Z Thursday.
